name: shinjuku-shielded

tools.name: shinjuku_setup
tools.description: The wallet is not set up on this machine yet. Call this when the user wants to pay an x402 URL, check a balance, or shield USDC. It asks the user to confirm in this client (with the spending caps), then creates a self-custody wallet on this machine (keys and a random passphrase in private local files; no tool takes or returns them), downloads and checks the proof tools (about 150 MB, minutes), and switches this server to the wallet tools. Takes no arguments. Call it again with no arguments as `next` says for the stage (confirming, platform, release, passphrase, wallet, proof-tools, config, done). A decline creates nothing (mcp_setup_declined). A client that cannot confirm is refused (mcp_setup_needs_terminal) with the terminal command.

annotations.title: Set up the Shinjuku Shielded wallet

tools.name: wallet_status
tools.description: Read only: whether the Shinjuku Shielded wallet is set up on this machine, what is missing, and the setup stage. Moves nothing.

tools.name: x402_discover
tools.description: Use this when you need a paid API for a job ("find a paid API for weather satellite images", "an x402 endpoint that returns token prices"). Pays nothing and signs nothing. Returns public x402 endpoints with url, method, description, and the listed price (atomic units: USDC 1000000 = 1 USDC). Endpoints this wallet can pay (Solana USDC, exact or shielded-exact) rank first among equal matches. Privacy: the public listings are downloaded in full and filtered on this machine, so no index learns what you searched for. The first call can take a minute or more (large listings); later calls use a local cache. A listed price is the listing's claim: call x402_preview on the url for the seller's real price before x402_pay.

query.description: A few words for what the API must do, e.g. "weather satellite image". Stays on this machine.

network.description: Rank endpoints on this network first: "solana" (default, the network this wallet pays on), "any", or a CAIP-2 id such as "eip155:8453".

instructions: A self-custody Shinjuku Shielded wallet server that is NOT SET UP on this machine yet. Every money tool answers wallet_not_set_up. When the user wants to pay, check a balance, or shield USDC, call shinjuku_setup: it asks the user to confirm in this client, then creates the wallet on this machine (the keys and a random passphrase stay in local files; no tool takes or returns them) and downloads and checks the proof tools. It takes minutes: call shinjuku_setup again as its answer's next says. When it answers stage done, the wallet tools are live in this same server (tools/list changes). A self-custody Shinjuku Shielded wallet on this machine; the keys and the passphrase stay in this process and no tool takes or returns them. Map the user's plain request to one tool: "what is my balance" -> wallet_balance; "shield 5 USDC" / "make my USDC private" -> wallet_shield; "shield the USDC in my Phantom / other agent wallet" -> wallet_shield_from_elsewhere (it answers an address and an exact amount; pay it with that wallet's own transfer tool, then call again; if the user changes their mind before paying, call it with action "cancel" and the same request_id); "pay this URL" -> x402_preview, then x402_pay; "find a paid API for X" -> x402_discover (the first call can take about 15 s or more while it downloads the public listings; your search words never leave this machine), then x402_preview on the url it found, then x402_pay; "send 2 USDC to <address>" -> wallet_unshield. wallet_balance answers ONE balance (balanceAtomic); breakdown names its parts. x402_pay pays any x402 seller from that one balance: a seller that takes only standard exact (Coinbase CDP, PayAI, ...) is paid through Shinjuku (the wallet pays Shinjuku privately, the seller's price plus a small fee, and Shinjuku pays the seller); x402_preview shows priceAtomic, feeAtomic, and totalAtomic, and max_payment_atomic must cover the total. If such a seller does not take the payment, the refund comes back to the balance by itself within about 7 minutes (it waits for the next pool anchor); nothing more to do. Amounts are atomic units (USDC: 1000000 = 1 USDC). The wallet does the upkeep by itself: it reads the chain when the local balance is stale and writes an encrypted backup after money moves; the user never runs a CLI command for this. wallet_shield, wallet_shield_from_elsewhere, and wallet_unshield run for minutes in the background: call again with the SAME request_id as each answer's next says; the same request_id never moves money twice. A send to an address that is not the wallet's own key or pre-approved by the owner asks the user to confirm it in this client first. x402_pay pays at most the per-payment cap set at launch and never more than the session cap. Never claim a payment happened unless the answer has a transaction. On an error code that ends in _retry_same_request, call x402_pay again with the SAME request_id: it never pays twice. Privacy: the payer is hidden in the shielded pool on chain, but this MCP host and its model provider see every URL, body, price, and paid answer the agent handles. Pool switches: when a tool answer has a poolSwitch field with tellUser true, tell the user each poolSwitch.items[].message where tellUser is true, in plain words, once. The wallet moves the balance by itself; the user never needs to act. During a switch the balance stays one number (balanceAtomic). wallet_move_status shows the details.
